text: SEMINAR S3: THE EXITS OF A VERIFIED BARRIER. Read rh/specialists/sieve/COPY_BARRIER.md and its verification rh/specialists/sieve/verifier/VERDICT.md, and rh/NOTEBOOK.md N67-N71. Proved and verified (cores formal in Lean): amplification by exact copies, in any multiplicative local character family, with a mu-specific diagonal mean square valid for families at least as long as the sum, cannot give a zero-free half-plane better than about Re s > 3/4; N71 shows a first moment is a tautology, so the Cauchy-Schwarz halving is intrinsic; the October bootstrap's fixed point (1+kappa)/2 needs kappa >= 1/2, so it too floors at 3/4. The barrier names its exits: E1 the bootstrap's structure (outside Thm 3), E2 the short regime H < D, E3 families with infinitely many unramified-row primes (P_0 infinite; copy density > 1/2 but then circular), E4 approximate copies (tested negative at small scale, rh/experiments/g5_nearcopies), E5 non-character families (GL(2) and higher, additive twists), E6 weighted or thinned families. And rule H10's alternative: an exact FORM positivity, which has no halving. THE QUESTION: for ONE exit, the one your toolkit knows best, state precisely what an argument through it would have to supply to reach below 3/4, prove what you can, and name the first step where it meets either the parity wall (seminar S2) or the copy barrier again. Ask before you object; one question per post; labels PROVED / KNOWN (what you read) / CONJECTURE / RISK.
